text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said Egypt's decision to hold the economic conference in Cairo -- in spite of difficulties in the peace process -- was the result of Egypt's conviction that holding it was preferable. He said that the conference, which President Hosni Mubarak will open on Tuesday morning, will confirm that what the region needs is cooperation based on peace and the conference is an important step towards that.

- President Hosni Mubarak will make a political speech this morning at a joint meeting of the two houses of parliament at the start of the new parliamentary session. The speech will deal with national action, development, encouraging investment, creating jobs and developing areas outside the Nile Valley.

- Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi announced that all security deaprtments have prepared to protect deelegations taking part in the economic conference. They will deal decisively with any attempt by anyone to cause trouble before or during the conference.

- Oil Minister Hamdi el-Banbi said that the chairmen of the biggest international oil companies will take part in the economic conference and talk about the advantages of investing in Egypt. In an interview with al-Ahram he said that several new petroleum projects would be announced during the conference, the most important of which are an ENI project worth $5 billion and a Shell project to develop its Western Desert fields at a cost of $570 million. The head of Amoco will announced a project to take Egyptian gas to Turkey.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri told a parliamentary meeting yesterday that the government was anxious not to pass any legislation that would add new burdens on the people.
- Ganzouri said that the new session of parliament would look at seven bills to bring about economic take-off.

- Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi issued a ministerial decree amending the rules for the residence of foreigners in Egypt. Foreign investors will receive five years' residence, provided they submit a letter from the General Organisation for Investment. Egyptians who gave up their Egyptian nationality to adopt another nationality will also get five years' residence.
- President Mubarak will open the economic conference at 11 a.m. on Tuesday before delegations from 72 countries.

- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said yesterday that the Palestinian people had a right to self-determination and to set up a state and that this was the only solution. Any other talk is unacceptable, he added.
